english_passage: The Yoruba people are an ethnic group that primarily inhabits West Africa. According to Yoruba mythology, the deity Obatala created the first human figurines out of earth in the sacred city of Ile-Ife, while the Supreme Creator, Olodumare, breathed the breath of life into them. english_passage: The Yoruba people are an ethnic group that primarily inhabits West Africa. The oldest known textual reference to the name Yoruba is found in a manuscript written by the scholar Ahmed Baba in the year 1614 in Timbuktu. The Yoruba indigenous religion is known as Isese, which encompasses traditional practices and beliefs. According to Yoruba mythology, the deity Obatala created the first human figurines out of earth in the sacred city of Ile-Ife, while the Supreme Creator, Olodumare, breathed the breath of life into them. Central to Yoruba philosophy is the concept of Omoluwabi, a guiding principle that dictates civilized behavior and good character. The term is derived from the phrase 'Omo + ti + Olu-iwa + bi', which conceptually identifies a person of exemplary virtue. An Omoluwabi demonstrates Iwapele, which signifies a set of values such as integrity, self-control, empathy, and hard work. This philosophical framework heavily influences traditional Yoruba art. Unlike Western aesthetic traditions, Yoruba art, including intricate textiles, often possesses a direct political and spiritual function, emphasizing the deep linguistic and cultural connection between visual artifacts and good moral character.
